edits.n: The perimeter of a square photo frame is 56 cm. What is the length of one side?

A square has four equal sides, so each side is 56 ÷ 4 = 14 cm. A divides by 2 as if only two sides counted, C divides the 40 but then appends the leftover 6 (10 + 6 = 16), and D subtracts 4 instead of dividing by 4.
divides perimeter by 2; subtracts instead of dividing
An L-shaped hallway floor is made of two rectangles: one is 9 m by 4 m and the other is 5 m by 3 m. What is the total area of the floor?

Add the two rectangle areas: 9 × 4 = 36 and 5 × 3 = 15, so 36 + 15 = 51 m². A adds the four dimensions instead of multiplying, B counts only the first rectangle, and C multiplies the combined lengths by the combined widths (14 × 7 = 98).
Which whole number multiplied by itself gives a product closest to 130?

11 × 11 = 121 is only 9 away from 130, while 12 × 12 = 144 is 14 away. A rounds 130 down to the benchmark 100 = 10 × 10, C picks the first square past 130 without comparing distances, and D comes from 130 ÷ 10.
uses 100 as benchmark; picks square above without comparing distances
A square rug has an area of 190 square feet. Its side length, in feet, is between which pair of consecutive whole numbers?

13 × 13 = 169 and 14 × 14 = 196, and 169 < 190 < 196, so the side is between 13 and 14. A halves 190 instead (9² = 81 and 10² = 100 surround 95), B stops after seeing 12² = 144 fall below 190, and C treats 14 as the lower bound once 14² passes 190.
halves instead of using squares; brackets off by one
A box holds 4 silver, 7 gold, and 9 copper coins. One coin is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is silver or gold?

There are 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 coins, and 4 + 7 = 11 of them are silver or gold, so the probability is 11/20. A uses only the silver coins (4/20 = 1/5), B uses only the gold coins, and C gives the probability of copper—the very coins the draw must avoid.
uses one category only; picks the excluded category
A box holds cards numbered 1 through 15. One card is drawn at random. What is the probability that the number drawn is greater than 9?

The favorable cards are 10 through 15—six of the 15—so the probability is 6/15 = 2/5. A counts the nine cards that are 9 or less (9/15 = 3/5), B wrongly includes the 9 itself (7/15), and D drops one favorable card (5/15 = 1/3).
counts the complement; boundary error with greater than
Two angles together form a straight line. One angle is 4 times as large as the other. What is the measure of the larger angle?

The two angles total 180° and make 5 equal parts, so the smaller is 180 ÷ 5 = 36° and the larger is 4 × 36 = 144°. A stops at the smaller angle, B divides 180 by 4 instead of 5, and C uses 90° as the total (4 × 18 = 72).
reports smaller angle; divides by 4; uses 90 as total
adds numerators and denominators; adds numerators without converting
Two angles are complementary. One angle measures 27°. What is the measure of the other angle?
Complementary angles total 90°, and 90−27=63°; C subtracts from 100, D subtracts from 180, and A slips by ten.

The first box holds 30 books on 5 shelves. The second box holds 42 books on 7 shelves. Which statement is true?
The first box holds more per shelf.
The second box holds 2 more per shelf.
The second box holds 12 more per shelf.

Both rates equal 6 books per shelf (30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6). A assumes fewer shelves means more on each shelf, C reports the difference in shelf counts (7 − 5 = 2) as a per-shelf difference, and D does the same with the totals (42 − 30 = 12).

Half the perimeter is 54 ÷ 2 = 27, so the width is 27 − 16 = 11. A reports only how much longer the length is than the width (16 − 11 = 5), B subtracts one length from the whole perimeter and halves what is left (54 − 16 = 38, then 19), and C subtracts both lengths but forgets to halve (54 − 32 = 22).

One lap is 2 × (30 + 18) = 96 m, and 1 3/4 × 96 = 168 m. A stops after one lap, B adds only one more 30 m side for the extra three-quarters of a lap (96 + 30 = 126), and C runs 1 1/2 laps instead of 1 3/4 (1.5 × 96 = 144).
stops after one lap; mishandles the fractional lap

Triangle angles total 180°, so 180 − (52 + 61) = 180 − 113 = 67°. D stops at the sum of the two given angles (113°), while A and C come from misadding 52 + 61 (as 123 or 103) before subtracting from 180°.
reports the two-angle sum; addition slips before subtracting

computes partial surface area; multiplication slips
Brisk means quick and energetic, as in a brisk walk; uneven, damp, and noisy describe other qualities, not speed.
To neglect is to fail to give proper care or attention, closest to ignore; damage may result but is not the action itself, and misplace concerns losing objects, not withholding attention.
The small nation wanted to write its own laws rather than follow another country's, so it declared itself ____.
Wanting to make its own laws leads a nation to declare itself independent; official, distant, and cheerful do not follow from that goal.
The ____ cook turned yesterday's rice and a few leftover vegetables into a delicious soup.
Turning leftovers into a good meal shows a resourceful cook; gentle, forgetful, and athletic do not explain making much from little.
Courageous means brave or fearless, willing to face danger; strength is physical, and wild and foolish describe poor judgment rather than courage.
Although the coach pointed out every mistake, Ellis gave a ____ reply and thanked her for the advice.
Accepting correction and thanking the coach shows a mature reply; boastful and stern clash with the thanks, and careless does not describe a considered response.
Slender means thin or slim in build; tall, elegant, and pale describe other qualities a slender thing need not have.
After the long morning hike, the campers were so ____ that they ate every sandwich in the basket.
A long hike explains why the campers were hungry enough to eat every sandwich; muddy, lost, and thirsty do not explain the eating.
Helmets are required at the bike park, but knee pads are ____; each rider chooses whether to wear them.
Since each rider chooses, the knee pads are optional, in contrast with required helmets; costly, modern, and popular do not describe something left to choice.
Ice creates a slipping risk, so walking slowly instead of rushing is the safe response; proudly, gracefully, and blindly do not address the danger.
Before confirmation, a surprising result should be considered uncertain; calling it final or accurate would skip the needed second test.
Returning money that is not his demonstrates honesty; curiosity, shyness, and cleverness do not explain the ethical choice.
Grandpa keeps his childhood drawings in a sealed box to ____ them for the family.
A sealed box helps preserve, or protect, the drawings for the future; measuring, releasing, or coloring them does not explain keeping them safe.
The mystery's first chapter was ____, but the ending explained everything.
But signals contrast with an ending that explained everything, so confusing fits; brief, complete, and familiar do not create that contrast.
The two recipes called for exactly the same ingredients and steps; there was no ____ between them.
Calling for exactly the same ingredients and steps means no difference; promise, distance, and purpose are not defined by the clue.
The sidewalk was still wet, so Milo stepped ____ around the puddles.
Meager means too small in amount, so small is closest; balanced, fresh, and useful do not indicate a lack.

Theo spent two days gluing foil stars and ribbons onto his kite. It rose, wobbled, and dove into the grass. His cousin Ada's plain paper kite climbed steadily. The wind was the same for both, so Theo stopped blaming it and watched. Ada's kite carried nothing extra except a long, light tail that kept its nose up. Theo pulled off the stars and ribbons and tied on a tail of folded paper bows. His kite lifted and flew. He kept one small ribbon on the handle, where its weight meant nothing to the sky, and decided to test his next kite before decorating it.

A limestone cave is not carved by one storm or earthquake. Most begin with rain. Rainwater sinking through soil collects a little carbon dioxide, making it slightly acidic. This water seeps into cracks in limestone and dissolves tiny bits of rock; over thousands of years, the cracks widen into tunnels and rooms. Even then, the water keeps working. Each drop falling from the ceiling leaves a speck of mineral, and the specks slowly build stone icicles called stalactites. Visitors see rock that looks finished, yet every tunnel is the sum of tiny changes.

[S1] Before the first permanent bridge crossed Silverbend River, ferries carried people, animals, and supplies between the two banks. [S2] Because the river bent sharply, a boat waiting at one landing could not see whether passengers had gathered at the other. [S3] In 1872, the ferry keeper and a shop owner created a simple signal: a red square raised on a pole meant that passengers were waiting, while a white square meant that freight needed space. [S4] The flags did not tell the ferryman exactly how many people or crates were present, but they helped him decide which boat to send. [S5] During fog, the system failed because neither bank could see the opposite pole, so workers rang a bell in agreed patterns instead. [S6] Old account books show fewer unnecessary crossings after the signals began. [S7] When a bridge finally opened, the flags disappeared, yet the idea behind them remained familiar: send only the information needed for the next decision.
